description:
Report of one emulation: the input metadata, the runs and the payloads.

Machine words are ``0x``-prefixed hex strings: addresses, pointers,
handles, raw argument values, return values, register values and exception
codes. A 64-bit word can be above 2**53 or 2**63, and JavaScript, Go
``interface{}``, jq and int64 stores such as SQLite lose such a value as a
JSON number with no error. Quantities, such as sizes, counts, offsets,
ticks and IDs, are JSON numbers.

A key is absent when Speakeasy did not collect its data. An empty list or
object means that Speakeasy collected the data and found nothing.

emulation_total_runtime.description: Wall-clock time in seconds, rounded to milliseconds, from the first start of the run queue to the end of the emulation.
emulation_total_runtime.title: Emulation Total Runtime

timestamp.description: Unix time in seconds of the first start of the run queue.
timestamp.title: Timestamp

path.description: Host path of the input file. Absent when the input came from bytes.
path.title: Path

size.description: Size of the input in bytes.
size.title: Size

image_base.description: Base address of the input image in the emulator. Rebase a disassembler database to this address to match the addresses of the report.
image_base.title: Image Base

errors.description: Errors that do not belong to one run, such as an ``invalid_image`` defect of the input PE.
errors.title: Errors

strings.description: Strings of the input and of memory. Only with ``analysis.strings``.

data.description: Payloads of the report, keyed by SHA-256. Each ``data_ref`` field holds a key of this mapping.
data.title: Data

entry_points.description: Runs of the emulation, in the order that the runs started.
entry_points.title: Entry Points

title: Report
